taxonomy.subtopic: IGF-1 elevation and failure of growth-hormone suppression after oral glucose

questions.stem_html: A 46-year-old man has progressive enlargement of his hands and feet, increased hat size, prognathism, diaphoresis, sleep apnea, and fasting hyperglycemia. Serum insulin-like growth factor 1 is above the age-adjusted range. Which result is expected during an oral glucose tolerance test?

options.text_html: Insulin-like growth factor 1 falls to an undetectable concentration within 30 minutes
Prolactin is completely suppressed in every affected patient
Growth hormone remains inadequately suppressed or may paradoxically rise despite hyperglycemia
Growth hormone-releasing hormone rises because hepatic feedback is absent
Cortisol fails to suppress after low-dose dexamethasone

questions.explanation_html: In healthy people, oral glucose suppresses growth-hormone secretion. A somatotroph adenoma secretes GH autonomously, so GH fails to suppress to the assay-specific nadir and can paradoxically increase. IGF-1 is the preferred screening measurement because it is more stable throughout the day.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: IGF-1 does not normally fall immediately after a glucose load and is used as an integrated marker of GH activity.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: Prolactin may be co-secreted by some pituitary adenomas, but complete suppression is not a diagnostic feature.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Most acromegaly is due to autonomous pituitary GH secretion rather than compensatory elevation of GHRH.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Failure of dexamethasone suppression evaluates hypercortisolism, not acromegaly.

questions.educational_objective: Use elevated IGF-1 and failure of oral-glucose-mediated GH suppression to confirm autonomous growth-hormone secretion in acromegaly.

media.alt_text: Use elevated IGF-1 and failure of oral-glucose-mediated GH suppression to confirm autonomous growth-hormone secretion in acromegaly.

taxonomy.subtopic: Ectopic endometrial glands and stroma with cyclic hemorrhage

questions.stem_html: A 31-year-old woman has infertility, deep dyspareunia, and pelvic pain that peaks during menstruation. Examination reveals tender nodularity in the posterior cul-de-sac. Laparoscopy shows blue-black peritoneal implants and an ovarian cyst filled with dark brown fluid. Which microscopic finding establishes the diagnosis?

options.text_html: Chorionic villi with trophoblastic proliferation
Mucin-producing epithelium with ovarian stromal invasion
Noncaseating granulomas confined to the fallopian tubes
Ectopic endometrial glands and stroma accompanied by hemorrhage and hemosiderin-laden macrophages
Intersecting fascicles of benign smooth muscle without endometrial tissue

questions.explanation_html: Endometriosis is defined histologically by endometrial glands and stroma outside the uterine cavity. Repeated cyclic bleeding produces fibrosis, old blood, and hemosiderin-laden macrophages, accounting for blue-black implants and an ovarian endometrioma.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Chorionic villi indicate an intrauterine or ectopic gestation rather than endometriosis.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: Invasive mucinous epithelium suggests an epithelial ovarian neoplasm.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Granulomatous salpingitis can impair fertility but does not cause cyclic hemorrhagic implants.

questions.educational_objective: Diagnose endometriosis by ectopic endometrial glands and stroma with cyclic hemorrhage, fibrosis, and hemosiderin-laden macrophages.

media.alt_text: Diagnose endometriosis by ectopic endometrial glands and stroma with cyclic hemorrhage, fibrosis, and hemosiderin-laden macrophages.

taxonomy.subtopic: ENaC-mediated lithium entry and aquaporin-2 downregulation

questions.stem_html: A 44-year-old woman with bipolar disorder treated with lithium has polyuria, intense thirst, serum sodium of 149 mEq/L, and urine osmolality of 108 mOsm/kg. Urine osmolality changes minimally after desmopressin. Amiloride is added. Which action makes this drug particularly useful in this setting?

options.text_html: Inhibition of the sodium-potassium-chloride cotransporter in the thick ascending limb
Direct agonism of vasopressin V2 receptors
Inhibition of carbonic anhydrase in the proximal tubule
Antagonism of aldosterone at the mineralocorticoid receptor
Blockade of epithelial sodium channels, reducing lithium entry into collecting-duct principal cells and limiting aquaporin-2 loss

questions.explanation_html: Lithium enters collecting-duct principal cells largely through ENaC and disrupts vasopressin signaling, reducing aquaporin-2 abundance and water permeability. Amiloride blocks ENaC, lowers intracellular lithium exposure, and can attenuate lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Loop-diuretic inhibition of NKCC2 reduces the medullary gradient but does not specifically block lithium entry into principal cells.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: The kidney is resistant to vasopressin signaling, so direct V2 stimulation does not correct the underlying lithium effect.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Carbonic-anhydrase inhibition causes bicarbonate diuresis and is not the targeted treatment for lithium entry.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonism does not prevent lithium passage through ENaC.

questions.educational_objective: Explain lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus through ENaC entry into principal cells, aquaporin-2 downregulation, and the targeted benefit of amiloride.

media.alt_text: Explain lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus through ENaC entry into principal cells, aquaporin-2 downregulation, and the targeted benefit of amiloride.

taxonomy.subtopic: Sodium-potassium ATPase inhibition and extracellular potassium shift

questions.stem_html: A 78-year-old man with chronic kidney disease takes digoxin for atrial fibrillation. After several days of poor oral intake, he develops nausea, confusion, yellow-tinted vision, bradycardia, and frequent ventricular ectopy. Serum potassium is 6.3 mEq/L. Which mechanism most directly accounts for the hyperkalemia?

options.text_html: Inhibition of sodium-potassium ATPase reduces active potassium uptake into cells
Opening of ATP-sensitive potassium channels causes rapid cellular potassium efflux
Suppression of aldosterone synthesis causes isolated distal potassium retention
Immune-mediated lysis of skeletal muscle releases intracellular potassium
Competitive inhibition of renal potassium secretion by digoxin metabolites

questions.explanation_html: Digoxin binds and inhibits the sodium-potassium ATPase. In acute or severe toxicity, reduced pump-mediated potassium entry into cells produces an extracellular potassium shift; hyperkalemia correlates with poisoning severity. The same pump inhibition raises intracellular sodium, decreases sodium-calcium exchange, and increases intracellular calcium, contributing to triggered arrhythmias.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: ATP-sensitive potassium-channel opening is not digoxin's mechanism.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Digoxin toxicity does not primarily suppress aldosterone production.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Rhabdomyolysis is not required to explain the potassium elevation.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: The principal mechanism is transcellular redistribution from pump inhibition rather than competitive blockade of tubular secretion.

questions.educational_objective: Connect severe digoxin toxicity to sodium-potassium ATPase inhibition, hyperkalemia, intracellular calcium loading, and arrhythmogenesis.

media.alt_text: Connect severe digoxin toxicity to sodium-potassium ATPase inhibition, hyperkalemia, intracellular calcium loading, and arrhythmogenesis.
